bibl.title: Choice-specific sequences in parietal cortex during a virtual-navigation decision task

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the temporal and anatomical structure of population activity in mouse posterior parietal cortex during a memory-guided choice
span.quote: The posterior parietal cortex (PPC) plays an important role in many cognitive behaviors; however, the neural circuit dynamics underlying PPC function are not well understood.

span.label: whether PPC dynamics are better described as classes of cells with sustained activity or as high-dimensional sequences
span.quote: We explored whether PPC dynamics are best described in terms of cell classes or high-dimensional dynamics. During a navigation-based decision task the dynamics were high-dimensional: neurons were active in choice-specific sequences in which information moves from one neuronal population to another across time in the task; although the neuronal activity patterns could be divided into cue, delay, and response groups, sequences were present within each group.

span.label: shows choice-specific sequences spanning the whole trial, implemented by cells anatomically intermixed below 100 microns, and argues this replaces the stable-state account
span.quote: During working memory decision tasks the PPC may therefore perform computations through sequence-based circuit dynamics, rather than long-lived stable states, implemented using anatomically intermingled microcircuits.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Distinct sequences of neurons were triggered on trials with opposite behavioral choices and defined divergent, choice-specific trajectories through a state space of neuronal population activity.

span.label: choice-specific neuronal sequences in posterior parietal cortex
span.quote: When the activity patterns of all the choice-specific, task-modulated cells were ordered according to the time profile of their Ca 2+ transients, the active periods across cells were staggered relative to one another in time forming a sequence of neuronal activation covering the entire trial length ( Fig. 2c–d , Supplementary Fig. 7c ).

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Similar choice-specific, task-modulated activity patterns were observed in extracellular electrophysiological recordings ( Supplementary Figs. 10–11 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A decision is reached when the evolving activity sequence intersects one of the choice-specific trajectories in population state space
span.quote: A decision is proposed to be reached when the sequence of activity intersects a choice-specific trajectory; different decisions involve intersections with different trajectories.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Growing state-space separation between the two choice trajectories over the trial progressively raises the barrier to reversing a decision
span.quote: Changing decisions would occur through transitions between trajectories, but as time progresses in the task, the state space distance between trajectories increases, in effect creating a larger barrier to change.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The parietal cortex switches between sustained-activity and sequence-based dynamical regimes according to the spatiotemporal demands of the behavioral task
span.quote: A possible explanation for heterogeneity and sequences in our experiments versus stereotypy and low-dimensional dynamics, which have been emphasized in previous recordings and models of PPC activity 1 , 13 – 18 , 20 – 21 , is that the PPC adopts different dynamics depending on the demands of the behavioral task.

span.label: information moves from one neuronal population to another across the trial, each cell active for only a fraction of it
span.quote: We explored whether PPC dynamics are best described in terms of cell classes or high-dimensional dynamics. During a navigation-based decision task the dynamics were high-dimensional: neurons were active in choice-specific sequences in which information moves from one neuronal population to another across time in the task; although the neuronal activity patterns could be divided into cue, delay, and response groups, sequences were present within each group.

span.label: a proposed framework: the sequence starts choice-independent, then moves toward one choice-specific trajectory, and the growing state-space distance between trajectories acts as a barrier to changing the decision
span.quote: Our results motivate consideration of a conceptual framework for decision-making and working memory in which sensory information used for the decision activates a neuronal sequence of activity. The sequence begins in a choice-independent state, which could be mediated by neurons that are not choice-specific ( Supplementary Fig. 7b ), and then moves toward a choice-specific trajectory and away from other trajectories in a manner dependent on the incoming information. A decision is proposed to be reached when the sequence of activity intersects a choice-specific trajectory; different decisions involve intersections with different trajectories. Upon reaching a decision, a working memory can be maintained by continuing along that choice-specific trajectory. Changing decisions would occur through transitions between trajectories, but as time progresses in the task, the state space distance between trajectories increases, in effect creating a larger barrier to change.

span.label: choice can be decoded from about 65 neurons within 250 microns, above chance in cue, delay and turn periods
span.quote: It was possible, from the activity of a small population of neurons located in close anatomical proximity (~65 neurons separated by < 250 µm), to predict the mouse’s choice on single correct trials at better than chance levels during the cue, delay, and turn periods

span.label: functionally distinct subnetworks are anatomically interlaced, implying highly specific synaptic connectivity rather than spatial clustering
span.quote: Because cells that were active at distinct time points in the task and that participated in different choice-specific sequences were spatially intermingled, our results indicate that functionally distinct subnetworks are anatomically interlaced in the PPC.

span.label: the mouse PPC is located first by retrograde and anterograde labelling, since the region had not been characterised in this species
span.quote: Because the location of the mouse PPC has not been characterized, we first performed retrograde and anterograde labeling experiments to locate it anatomically ( Methods, Supplementary Fig. 4 ). We identified a region consistent with the rat and primate PPC based on the set of areas from where it received axonal projections, the areas to which it sent projections, and its location relative to other cortical regions 8 , 34 (anterior to visual cortex and posterior to somatosensory cortex). We therefore considered this area to be the mouse PPC.

span.label: necessity established by muscimol inactivation, with a visually-guided version of the task as the control for visual and motor deficits
span.quote: In contrast, PPC inactivation did not significantly affect performance on a visually-guided task in which a visual cue was present at the reward site and visible throughout the trial, indicating that the decrease in performance on the memory-guided task was unlikely due to a major visual or motor deficit

span.label: trials aligned to cue offset, turn onset and trial end, because running speed and turn position varied across trials and mice
span.quote: To compare behaviorally similar epochs of the task across trials, individual trials were aligned to the time points when the cue was no longer visible (cue offset), the turn onset, and the end of the trial; these alignment points formed the boundaries of cue (trial start to cue offset: 5.1 ± 2.6 s), delay (cue offset to turn onset: 4.2 ± 1.2 s), and turn task periods (turn onset to trial end: 3.0

span.label: The task confounds the decision with ongoing navigation, so the decision process itself was not isolated.
span.quote: Our behavioral paradigm did not isolate the decision-making process.

span.label: Whether the sequences serve decision-related processes remains to be tested.
span.quote: Sequences may therefore play a role in some aspect of decision-related processes, but further experiments will be necessary to assess this possibility.

span.label: The weak distance-dependence of pairwise correlation may be an optical artefact rather than real spatial organisation.
span.quote: This weak relationship could be due to overlapping fluorescence changes, such as from dendritic signals, or could reflect an actual, weak spatial organization.

span.label: The result may not generalise across PPC regions, layers or species.
span.quote: In addition, different regions or layers of the PPC may have differing activity dynamics 45 , or the dynamics of rodent and primate PPC circuits may differ.

span.label: the paradigm does not isolate decision-making, so the role of sequences in the decision itself is untested
span.quote: Our behavioral paradigm did not isolate the decision-making process. We note however that activity trajectories occasionally switched during a trial between the prototypical correct left and right choice trajectories, including frequently on error trials, suggesting that the mouse’s decision was not necessarily irreversibly reached immediately after a trial’s start (trajectory selectivity switch during the delay period or last 1 s of the cue period: 63% of error trials, 20% of correct trials; Fig. 4d,g , Supplementary Fig. 19e–f ). Sequences may therefore play a role in some aspect of decision-related processes, but further experiments will be necessary to assess this possibility.

span.label: the weak distance-correlation relationship may be overlapping fluorescence rather than real spatial organisation, and the paper declines to choose
span.quote: This weak relationship could be due to overlapping fluorescence changes, such as from dendritic signals, or could reflect an actual, weak spatial organization.

span.label: four rival explanations are offered for why this result differs from the primate literature and none is selected
span.quote: Alternatively, sequences of activity may be present in the primate PPC during traditional tasks but have yet to be identified, consistent with emerging evidence for heterogeneous temporal response properties 22 – 24 , 30 . In addition, different regions or layers of the PPC may have differing activity dynamics 45 , or the dynamics of rodent and primate PPC circuits may differ.

span.label: spatial and temporal progression through the task were highly correlated, so what the active cell encodes cannot be separated
span.quote: Our results also offer a way to unite previous work on neural coding in the PPC. Navigation, memory, and choice information may be combined in the sequences such that the identity of the active sequence reflects choice-related information for working memory and movement planning 4 – 5 and the currently active cell within the sequence reflects spatial or temporal progression through the task 7 , 43 , which were highly correlated in our task

span.label: the mouse PPC is a stipulated region, defined by projection pattern and position rather than by any functional criterion
span.quote: Because the location of the mouse PPC has not been characterized, we first performed retrograde and anterograde labeling experiments to locate it anatomically ( Methods, Supplementary Fig. 4 ). We identified a region consistent with the rat and primate PPC based on the set of areas from where it received axonal projections, the areas to which it sent projections, and its location relative to other cortical regions 8 , 34 (anterior to visual cortex and posterior to somatosensory cortex). We therefore considered this area to be the mouse PPC.

span.label: the state-space trajectory view of population activity, taken explicitly from work on behavioural choice in the leech nervous system
span.quote: Our results motivate consideration of a conceptual framework for decision-making and working memory in which sensory information used for the decision activates a neuronal sequence of activity. The sequence begins in a choice-independent state, which could be mediated by neurons that are not choice-specific ( Supplementary Fig. 7b ), and then moves toward a choice-specific trajectory and away from other trajectories in a manner dependent on the incoming information. A decision is proposed to be reached when the sequence of activity intersects a choice-specific trajectory; different decisions involve intersections with different trajectories. Upon reaching a decision, a working memory can be maintained by continuing along that choice-specific trajectory. Changing decisions would occur through transitions between trajectories, but as time progresses in the task, the state space distance between trajectories increases, in effect creating a larger barrier to change.

span.label: feedforward architectures and liquid state machines, offered as possible implementations
span.quote: During working memory decision tasks the PPC may therefore perform computations through sequence-based circuit dynamics, rather than long-lived stable states, implemented using anatomically intermingled microcircuits.

span.label: sequence here means each neuron active for only a fraction of a task period with different cells active at different times - explicitly opposed to a class of cells sharing one time course
span.quote: Sequences suggest dynamics that are high-dimensional, without the presence of classes of cells with relatively homogeneous activity time courses.

span.label: high-dimensional vs low-dimensional is used as the criterion separating the two accounts: low-dimensional means each cell's activity is an amplitude-scaled copy of one prototypical time series
span.quote: The low-dimensional dynamics can be reproduced in recurrent attractor network models, in which each cell’s activity is typically an amplitude-scaled version of a prototypical time series

span.label: delay cell, cue cell and response cell are treated as possibly artifactual categories - the paper finds the three groups but shows sequences inside each one
span.quote: Although the population of neurons could be divided into groups, the temporal activity patterns within each individual period were heterogeneous and formed sequences

span.label: mouse PPC is a stipulated object: the region was located by its afferents, efferents and position relative to visual and somatosensory cortex, then declared to be PPC
span.quote: Because the location of the mouse PPC has not been characterized, we first performed retrograde and anterograde labeling experiments to locate it anatomically ( Methods, Supplementary Fig. 4 ). We identified a region consistent with the rat and primate PPC based on the set of areas from where it received axonal projections, the areas to which it sent projections, and its location relative to other cortical regions 8 , 34 (anterior to visual cortex and posterior to somatosensory cortex). We therefore considered this area to be the mouse PPC.

span.quote: At each time point, the activity

span.label: extends → previous work on spatial intermixing of response properties in sensory cortex, motor cortex and hippocampus (refs 12, 31–32)
span.quote: This extends previous work in sensory cortex, motor cortex, and the hippocampus showing spatial intermixing of heterogeneous response properties in cells encoding qualitatively similar types of information (e.g. orientation selectivity in visual cortex) or cells with activity during similar task epochs 12 , 31 – 32 .

span.label: contradicts → models predicting spatial clustering of similar response patterns and connectivity from axonal-dendritic overlap (refs 46–47)
span.note: differs in: spatial clustering and connectivity rule: the opposing models EMPHASIZED THE SPATIAL CLUSTERING OF SIMILAR RESPONSE PATTERNS, AS IN FUNCTIONAL COLUMNS, AND PROPOSE CONNECTIVITY DEFINED BY AXONAL-DENDRITIC OVERLAP WITHOUT FINE-SCALE SPECIFICITY
span.quote: These findings differ from the predictions of models that have emphasized the spatial clustering of similar response patterns, as in functional columns, and that propose connectivity defined by axonal-dendritic overlap without fine-scale specificity 46 – 47 .

span.label: builds-on → studies identifying cortical sequences of activity states during working memory tasks (refs 27–30)
span.quote: The choice-specific sequences of PPC neuronal activation we report here add to the growing list of studies that have identified cortical sequences of activity states during working memory tasks 27 – 30 .

span.label: extends → the trajectory account of behavioural choice first developed for the leech nervous system (ref. 37)
span.quote: The framework we propose is an extension of a point-of-view first considered in describing the dynamics underlying behavioral choices in the leech nervous system 37 .

span.label: contradicts → the account of PPC as classes of cells with sustained activity spanning whole task periods
span.note: differs in: homogeneous classes against sequences: CLASSES OF CELLS WITH HOMOGENEOUS ACTIVITY PATTERNS WERE NOT PRESENT. RATHER, CHOICE-SPECIFIC SEQUENCES OF NEURONS WERE ACTIVATED IN ALL BEHAVIORAL PERIODS
span.quote: Together these data indicate that classes of cells with homogeneous activity patterns were not present. Rather, choice-specific sequences of neurons were activated in all behavioral periods, with a lower density of cells in the sequence at the borders between periods.

span.label: contradicts → models predicting spatial clustering of similar response patterns, as in functional columns
span.note: differs in: the same parameter as item 1 - spatial clustering, AS IN FUNCTIONAL COLUMNS, against fine-scale specificity
span.quote: These findings differ from the predictions of models that have emphasized the spatial clustering of similar response patterns, as in functional columns, and that propose connectivity defined by axonal-dendritic overlap without fine-scale specificity

span.label: extends → reports of cortical activity sequences during working memory in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus
span.quote: In addition, there is growing evidence for sequences of neuronal activation within local circuits, in which each neuron is active for only a fraction of a task period, including during working memory tasks in the prefrontal cortex 25 – 28 and the hippocampus 29 and during an object construction task in the PPC

span.label: distinguishes-from → hippocampal place cells, since PPC cells did not encode location on a linear track
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS A SPECIFIC TASK THAT SEPARATES THEM. 'IT SEEMS UNLIKELY THAT PPC NEURONS ONLY PROVIDED LOCATION INFORMATION IN A CONTEXT-DEPENDENT MANNER, LIKE HIPPOCAMPAL PLACE CELLS, BECAUSE UNLIKE PLACE CELLS PPC NEURONS DID NOT ENCODE SPATIAL LOCATION DURING A LINEAR TRACK TASK.' The distinction is drawn by a task the alternative account predicts they would pass - so the axis names the experiment that discriminates, not a property of either population. Q-494.
span.quote: It seems unlikely that PPC neurons only provided location information in a context-dependent manner, like hippocampal place cells 29 , 44 , because unlike place cells PPC neurons did not encode spatial location during a linear track task

span.label: qualifies → drift-diffusion and recurrent winner-take-all models of decision-making
span.note: differs in: what the dynamics settle into: DECISIONS ARE REACHED WHEN THE ACTIVITY APPROACHES A CHOICE-SPECIFIC FIXED POINT WITH WORKING MEMORY MAINTAINED AS STABLE ACTIVITY AT THAT POINT, and THE TRAJECTORIES ARE DEFINED BY RELATIVELY HOMOGENEOUS changes - against a sequence
span.quote: However, these models differ from the sequence framework in that decisions are reached when the activity approaches a choice-specific fixed point with working memory maintained as stable activity at that point. Thus, although these circuits can demonstrate divergent trajectories to reach the fixed points associated with different choices, the trajectories are defined by relatively homogeneous changes in the activity of the population, and the same set of neurons participate in all stages of the decision-making and working memory process.

span.label: reconciles → the primate literature reporting persistent activity, by proposing the task demands select the dynamics
span.note: differs in: the task the animal was doing: THE PPC ADOPTS DIFFERENT DYNAMICS DEPENDING ON THE DEMANDS OF THE BEHAVIORAL TASK, which is offered as the explanation for HETEROGENEITY AND SEQUENCES IN OUR EXPERIMENTS VERSUS STEREOTYPY AND LOW-DIMENSIONAL DYNAMICS
span.quote: A possible explanation for heterogeneity and sequences in our experiments versus stereotypy and low-dimensional dynamics, which have been emphasized in previous recordings and models of PPC activity 1 , 13 – 18 , 20 – 21 , is that the PPC adopts different dynamics depending on the demands of the behavioral task.

span.label: sequence of neuronal activation —contrasted-with→ sustained firing rate changes
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the paper's whole question is which of these two descriptions fits
span.quote: Sequences suggest dynamics that are high-dimensional, without the presence of classes of cells with relatively homogeneous activity time courses.

span.label: low-dimensional —operationalised-as→ recurrent attractor network models
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — the model is what makes the dimensionality claim testable - each cell an amplitude-scaled copy of one time series
span.quote: The low-dimensional dynamics can be reproduced in recurrent attractor network models, in which each cell’s activity is typically an amplitude-scaled version of a prototypical time series

span.label: sequence of neuronal activation —causes→ high-dimensional
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — sequences SUGGEST high-dimensional dynamics; the weight carries the hedge
span.quote: Sequences suggest dynamics that are high-dimensional, without the presence of classes of cells with relatively homogeneous activity time courses.

span.label: choice-specific cells —part-of→ task-modulated cells
span.quote: The majority (~71%) of task-modulated cells had significantly different levels of activity on correct right and left choice trials (choice-specific cells).

span.label: PPC —distinct-from→ place cells
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS A NEGATIVE TEST USED TO RULE OUT AN ALTERNATIVE. 'IT SEEMS UNLIKELY THAT PPC NEURONS ONLY PROVIDED LOCATION INFORMATION IN A CONTEXT-DEPENDENT MANNER, LIKE HIPPOCAMPAL PLACE CELLS, BECAUSE UNLIKE PLACE CELLS PPC NEURONS DID NOT ENCODE SPATIAL LOCATION DURING A LINEAR TRACK TASK.' The comparison is not offered as a finding about PPC - it is offered as the reason a competing interpretation fails, so the axis is what the alternative would have predicted. Q-485. · strength of the relation: 0.9 — argued from a negative result on a linear track, not from a positive dissociation
span.quote: It seems unlikely that PPC neurons only provided location information in a context-dependent manner, like hippocampal place cells 29 , 44 , because unlike place cells PPC neurons did not encode spatial location during a linear track task
